epic.title: epic-418-followon — make agents use the MCP door instead of the CLI
epic.intent_and_why: Agents drive their spines through the MCP door and never touch the engine CLI directly; the CLI is an implementation detail behind the door. Entry definitions stay configurable so the work is OS-agnostic by construction. Anything an operator must remember to do by hand is a defect in the tool.

definition_of_done: A dispatched crew drives its own spine through the door, measured from its own call record.
A respawned agent on the same assignment resumes its lease rather than force-claiming it.
Constellation agent instructions name the door and not the engine CLI.
No shipped entry definition hardcodes an interpreter or an absolute path.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: Every claim about what happened brings its evidence; a control must reproduce the defect before a fix is believed.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Measured from the driving agent's own call record, never from the engine's refusals counter.
good_enough.appetite: One bounded wave; keep out the easy failures rather than making it foolproof.

hard_constraints: docs/agents/* edits are a human's call
No merge or push to main while the human is AFK
Planning makes no direct gh or network mutation
fixed_decisions: The lease keys on the assignment, not the process instance
Identity is derived from the spine's own work_id, never hand-typed
Every spine action is reachable through the MCP door; a CLI-only verb is a defect
Agents do not know about the engine CLI; the CLI is used only behind the MCP door
Mechanical setup is the tool's job, not the operator's
Hardcoding an interpreter for the current host is permitted provided every instance is recorded on #539, which carries the unified cross-platform fix

current_wave.objective: Make running things require no thought: the launcher grants what a crew needs, entry definitions resolve per machine, and the documentation stops being wrong.
exit_criteria: A crew dispatched through run_crew.py receives its tools and permission mode from the launcher, with no hand-written per-dispatch settings file required.
No shipped entry definition hardcodes an interpreter; the value resolves per machine at install time and the committed file still works as committed.
docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md's Python guidance teaches a reader to measure their own host rather than restating another host's answer.
A cold reviewer independent of the implementer has approved each change.
#555 is carried unchanged and unworked; its terms are preserved verbatim, no spend is authorized against it, and its disposition returns to the human.

wave_evidence.claim: Agents choose the CLI even when the door is bound for them
wave_evidence.expected: A correctly bound crew still prefers the CLI, so adoption needs more than binding
wave_evidence.observed: RETRACTED, and the opposite is now measured. grep SPINE_FILE across this epic's ten dispatch scripts: one BOUND, nine UNBOUND. Every crew previously read as 'choosing the CLI' had a door bound to a wave-1 scratch demo spine, so the CLI was the only path to its own spine. After M1 merged, the very next two dispatches -- with no SPINE_FILE in their scripts -- drove their whole spines through the door, one of them a reviewer, with zero CLI calls.
wave_evidence.source: the ten *-dispatch.sh scripts; mcp_calls.jsonl and the engine_session block of REPAIR_PLAN.json and REVIEW_SURVEY.json

wave_evidence.claim: Binding the door is sufficient for adoption
wave_evidence.expected: A bound crew uses the door
wave_evidence.observed: SUPPORTED so far, on two of two post-M1 dispatches, both of which also released their leases. Two dispatches is a weak base and the CLI remained reachable to both, so this does not yet separate 'the door is convenient' from 'the door is the only thing bound'. N2 removes that confound by withholding the engine.

wave_evidence.claim: A tracked config may never name an interpreter (#539)
wave_evidence.expected: Shipping a placeholder is strictly safer than shipping a name
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED as stated. The placeholder broke test_mcp_spine_server.py's var-expansion launch test, which starts a real server from the committed .mcp.json. The rule needs a second half: a tracked config that code also reads directly must be launchable as committed, and the per-machine correction belongs at install time.
wave_evidence.source: the failing test on 7995ec5e; the human's ruling of 2026-08-10; #539 comment 5248339534

wave_evidence.claim: Omitting a tool from the crew allow-list withholds the capability
wave_evidence.expected: Not granting the engine withholds the engine
wave_evidence.observed: FALSE. CREW_ALLOWED_TOOLS grants unrestricted Bash, which reaches checklist_engine.py regardless of which MCP tools are granted. N2 needs a real mechanism, not an omission.
wave_evidence.source: the M2 cold reviewer's out-of-scope observations
